mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals a strong accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which often precedes economic downturns and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.2% change), it indicates strong demand without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% MoM and CPIAUCSL changes < 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% and CPIAUCSL changes by less than 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment (PAYEMS) and stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE stable (changes < 0.1% MoM)
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% and UNRATE remains stable month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% is associated with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of economic expansion, a significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) coupled with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates strong economic fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% QoQ and UNRATE stable (changes < 0.2% MoM)
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE remains stable month-over-month.
